fixFirst.title: HTTP is not upgraded to HTTPS
fixFirst.fix: Install a certificate, serve the site over HTTPS, and redirect every HTTP address to its HTTPS version.

fixFirst.title: Broken internal link
fixFirst.fix: Fix the link to point at a working page, or restore the missing page and redirect it if it moved.

fixFirst.title: HTML is served without compression
fixFirst.fix: Turn on gzip or Brotli compression for HTML responses in the web server or CDN.

fixFirst.title: A noindex page is listed in the sitemap
fixFirst.fix: Remove the page from the sitemap, or remove the noindex directive.

fixFirst.title: Page has no title
fixFirst.fix: Add a unique <title> that describes the page in about 50 to 60 characters.

checks.title: Page has no title
checks.why: The title is the main heading shown in search results and browser tabs. Without one, search engines pick their own text.
checks.fix: Add a unique <title> that describes the page in about 50 to 60 characters.

findings.detail: No <title> element, or it is empty.

checks.title: Title is very short or very long
checks.why: Very short titles say little about the page. Search results cut long titles off, so the end may never be seen.
checks.fix: Aim for a title between 10 and 60 characters that puts the main words first.

checks.title: Title is shared with other pages
checks.why: Pages with the same title are hard to tell apart in search results and in browser tabs.
checks.fix: Give each page its own title that describes what is unique about it.

findings.detail: Title is shared with 1 other indexable page.
Title is shared with 1 other indexable page.

checks.title: Page has more than one title
checks.why: Browsers and search engines have to choose between the titles, and they may choose the wrong one.
checks.fix: Keep a single <title> element in the document head and remove the rest.

checks.title: Page has no meta description
checks.why: Search engines often use the meta description as the snippet under the title. Without one they choose text from the page.
checks.fix: Add a <meta name="description"> that summarises the page in one or two sentences.

checks.title: Meta description is very short or very long
checks.why: A very short description gives searchers little reason to click. Search results cut long descriptions off.
checks.fix: Write a description between 50 and 160 characters that says what the page offers.

findings.detail: Meta description is 40 characters long. A typical range is 50 to 160.

checks.title: Meta description is shared with other pages
checks.why: Identical descriptions make different pages look the same in search results.
checks.fix: Write a description for each page that reflects its own content.

findings.detail: Meta description is shared with 1 other indexable page.
Meta description is shared with 1 other indexable page.

checks.title: Page has no h1 heading
checks.why: The h1 tells readers and search engines what the page is about.
checks.fix: Add one <h1> that states the topic of the page.

checks.title: Page has more than one h1 heading
checks.why: HTML allows more than one h1, but a single one keeps the page outline clear for readers and search engines.
checks.fix: Use one <h1> for the page topic and <h2> or lower for sections.

findings.detail: The page has 2 <h1> headings.

checks.title: Page has no canonical link
checks.why: A canonical link tells search engines which URL to index when the same content is reachable at several addresses.
checks.fix: Add <link rel="canonical"> pointing at the preferred URL of the page, usually the page itself.

checks.title: Page has conflicting canonical links
checks.why: When the canonical links disagree, search engines may ignore them and choose for themselves.
checks.fix: Keep one canonical link per page. Check whether a plugin or theme adds a second one.

checks.title: Canonical points to a broken or redirecting URL
checks.why: A canonical that does not return a normal page sends search engines to a dead end, so the page may drop out of the index.
checks.fix: Point the canonical at the final URL of a page that returns status 200.

checks.title: Canonical points to a different origin
checks.why: A canonical on another host or scheme asks search engines to index that other site instead of this page.
checks.fix: Use a canonical on the same scheme and host as the page, unless the move is intended.

checks.title: Page is set to noindex
checks.why: Search engines will not list a noindex page. This is listed so you can confirm it is intended.
checks.fix: If the page should appear in search, remove the noindex directive from the meta robots tag and the X-Robots-Tag header.

findings.detail: The page carries a noindex directive.

checks.title: A noindex page is listed in the sitemap
checks.why: The sitemap says the page should be indexed while the page says it should not, so the two signals contradict each other.
checks.fix: Remove the page from the sitemap, or remove the noindex directive.

findings.detail: The page is noindex but is listed in the sitemap.

checks.title: A sitemap URL is blocked by robots.txt
checks.why: The sitemap offers a URL that robots.txt forbids crawlers to fetch. Search engines cannot read a page they may not crawl.
checks.fix: Remove the URL from the sitemap, or change the robots.txt rule that blocks it.

checks.title: The start page is set to noindex
checks.why: A noindex start page keeps the home of the site out of search results.
checks.fix: Remove the noindex directive from the start page meta robots tag and X-Robots-Tag header.

checks.title: Page has no lang attribute
checks.why: The lang attribute tells browsers, search engines and screen readers which language the page is in.
checks.fix: Add a lang attribute to the <html> element, for example <html lang="en">.

checks.title: Page has no viewport meta tag
checks.why: Without a viewport tag, phones show the page zoomed out as a desktop layout, which is hard to read and use.
checks.fix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> to the head.

checks.title: Open Graph tags are missing
checks.why: Open Graph tags control the title, text and image shown when the page is shared on social networks and in chat apps.
checks.fix: Add og:title, og:description and og:image meta tags to the head.

findings.detail: Missing og:title, og:description, og:image.
Missing og:title, og:description, og:image.

checks.title: Structured data is not valid JSON
checks.why: Search engines skip a JSON-LD block they cannot parse, so the page loses any rich results it was meant to earn.
checks.fix: Fix the syntax of the JSON-LD block. A JSON validator will point at the error.

findings.detail: A JSON-LD block is not valid JSON.

checks.title: No robots.txt file
checks.why: Crawlers look for robots.txt first. Without one they assume everything may be crawled and they cannot find the sitemap from it.
checks.fix: Publish a robots.txt at the root of the site, even a short one that links to the sitemap.

findings.detail: robots.txt returned status 404.

checks.title: robots.txt blocks the whole site
checks.why: It tells search engine crawlers not to fetch any page of the site.
checks.fix: Remove the Disallow: / rule for the all-crawlers group, unless the site is meant to stay private.

checks.title: robots.txt returns a server error
checks.why: When robots.txt answers with a server error, search engines may stop crawling the site until it recovers.
checks.fix: Make robots.txt answer with status 200, or status 404 if you have none. Check the server logs for the error.

checks.title: No sitemap found
checks.why: A sitemap helps search engines find every page, especially new pages and pages with few links to them.
checks.fix: Publish a sitemap.xml and list it in robots.txt.

checks.title: robots.txt does not reference the sitemap
checks.why: A Sitemap line in robots.txt lets every crawler find the sitemap without being told about it.
checks.fix: Add a line such as Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml to robots.txt.

findings.detail: A sitemap exists but robots.txt has no Sitemap line.

checks.title: A sitemap URL does not return status 200
checks.why: The sitemap should list only live pages. Broken or redirecting entries waste crawl effort.
checks.fix: Remove the URL from the sitemap, or list its final address.

checks.title: A sitemap file could not be parsed
checks.why: Search engines ignore a sitemap they cannot read, so none of its URLs are submitted.
checks.fix: Check that the file is valid sitemap XML and is served with status 200.

checks.title: A sitemap URL is not linked from any crawled page
checks.why: A page that nothing links to is hard for visitors and crawlers to reach. It may be an orphan.
checks.fix: Link the page from a relevant page or the navigation, or remove it from the sitemap if it is retired.

checks.title: Page has little text
checks.why: Pages with very little text give search engines little to rank. Some pages, such as contact or gallery pages, are fine this way.
checks.fix: If the page should rank, add useful text that answers what visitors come for.

checks.title: Broken internal link
checks.why: Visitors and search engines who follow the link reach an error page instead of content.
checks.fix: Fix the link to point at a working page, or restore the missing page and redirect it if it moved.

findings.detail: The URL returns status 404.

checks.title: Internal link points at a redirect
checks.why: Each redirect adds a round trip for visitors and crawlers.
checks.fix: Update the link to point straight at the final address.

findings.detail: Redirects to http://127.0.0.1:4173/about
Redirects to http://127.0.0.1:4173/dup-a

checks.title: Redirect chain has more than one hop
checks.why: Every extra hop slows the page down and gives crawlers another chance to give up.
checks.fix: Redirect the first address straight to the final address.

findings.detail: Redirect chain of 2 hops ending at http://127.0.0.1:4173/dup-a.

checks.title: Redirect loop or too many redirects
checks.why: Browsers and crawlers give up on a loop, so the page cannot be reached at all.
checks.fix: Remove the redirect that points back at an earlier address in the chain.

checks.title: HTTP is not upgraded to HTTPS
checks.why: Plain HTTP traffic can be read and changed on the way, and browsers label such sites as not secure.
checks.fix: Install a certificate, serve the site over HTTPS, and redirect every HTTP address to its HTTPS version.

findings.detail: The site is served over plain HTTP.

checks.title: Mixed content on an HTTPS page
checks.why: Browsers block or warn about resources loaded over HTTP on a secure page, so the page can look broken.
checks.fix: Change the resource addresses to HTTPS, or remove them.

checks.title: HTTPS page links to an internal page over HTTP
checks.why: Visitors who follow the link leave the secure version of the site and may hit an extra redirect.
checks.fix: Change the link to use https://.

checks.title: www and apex hosts both answer without a redirect
checks.why: Two hosts serving the same site can split links and ranking signals between them, and create duplicate pages.
checks.fix: Pick one host as the main one and redirect the other to it.

checks.title: Missing pages return 200 (soft 404)
checks.why: Search engines may index error pages as real content, and broken links are harder to find.
checks.fix: Make the server return status 404 for addresses that do not exist.

checks.title: No favicon
checks.why: Browsers ask for a favicon to show in tabs and bookmarks. Without one they show a generic icon, and the requests end in 404 errors.
checks.fix: Add a favicon link to the page head, or serve a file at /favicon.ico.

findings.detail: No favicon link in the pages and no /favicon.ico file.

checks.title: No Strict-Transport-Security header
checks.why: Without this header, browsers may still try plain HTTP first, which leaves a window for downgrade attacks.
checks.fix: Send Strict-Transport-Security with a max-age of at least six months on every HTTPS response.

checks.title: No Content-Security-Policy header
checks.why: A content security policy limits where scripts and other resources can load from, which reduces the damage of injected code.
checks.fix: Add a Content-Security-Policy header. Start in report-only mode if the site loads many third-party resources.

findings.detail: The start page has no Content-Security-Policy header. 8 other pages also lack it.

checks.title: No X-Content-Type-Options nosniff header
checks.why: Without nosniff, some browsers guess file types and may run a file as a script when it was not meant to be one.
checks.fix: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response.

findings.detail: The start page has no X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header. 8 other pages also lack it.

checks.title: No Referrer-Policy header
checks.why: Without a policy, browsers decide how much of the page address is shared with other sites when a visitor clicks a link.
checks.fix: Send a Referrer-Policy header such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin.

findings.detail: The start page has no Referrer-Policy header. 8 other pages also lack it.

checks.title: No clickjacking protection
checks.why: Without X-Frame-Options or a frame-ancestors rule, other sites can embed the page in a frame and trick visitors into clicking hidden controls.
checks.fix: Send X-Frame-Options or add a frame-ancestors rule to the Content-Security-Policy.

findings.detail: The start page has no X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors header. 8 other pages also lack it.

checks.title: Broken external link
checks.why: Links that lead nowhere frustrate visitors and make the site look neglected.
checks.fix: Update or remove the link.

checks.title: Page timed out or was cut short
checks.why: The audit only saw part of the page, and slow pages are also slow for visitors and crawlers.
checks.fix: Check the server for slow responses, and reduce the page size if it hit the size cap.

checks.title: Slow server response
checks.why: A slow first response delays everything that follows, and visitors notice.
checks.fix: Look at server work before the HTML is sent: slow queries, missing page caching, or an underpowered host.

checks.title: HTML document is very large
checks.why: Large documents take longer to download and parse, especially on slow mobile connections.
checks.fix: Remove inline data and repeated markup, and load long lists in parts.

checks.title: HTML is served without compression
checks.why: Compression usually cuts the size of HTML by a large share, so pages download faster.
checks.fix: Turn on gzip or Brotli compression for HTML responses in the web server or CDN.

findings.detail: The 1119 byte HTML response has no gzip, br, deflate or zstd encoding.

checks.title: Script or stylesheet served without compression
checks.why: Text assets compress well. Sending them as they are wastes bandwidth and slows rendering.
checks.fix: Turn on gzip or Brotli compression for JavaScript and CSS files.

findings.detail: The 2640 byte stylesheet has no compression.

checks.title: Static asset is not cached for long
checks.why: Without a cache lifetime, returning visitors download the same files again on every visit.
checks.fix: Send Cache-Control with a max-age of at least one hour, and a year for files whose names change when they change.

findings.detail: No Cache-Control or Expires header.
No Cache-Control or Expires header.

checks.title: Page is heavy
checks.why: Heavy pages load slowly on mobile connections and use up visitors' data.
checks.fix: Compress and resize images first, then remove scripts and fonts the page does not need.

checks.title: Page is very heavy
checks.why: Pages this large take a long time to load on slow connections and use a lot of mobile data.
checks.fix: Compress and resize images first, then remove scripts and fonts the page does not need.

checks.title: Page references many resources
checks.why: Each script, stylesheet and image is another request, which adds delay on slow connections.
checks.fix: Combine small files, drop unused ones, and lazy load images below the fold.

checks.title: Large image
checks.why: Images are often the largest part of a page.
checks.fix: Resize the image to the size it is shown at and compress it, or use a modern format such as WebP or AVIF.

findings.detail: The image is 600000 bytes.

checks.title: Very large image
checks.why: An image this large can take seconds to load and uses a lot of mobile data.
checks.fix: Resize the image to the size it is shown at and compress it, or use a modern format such as WebP or AVIF.

checks.title: Images without width and height
checks.why: Without both attributes the browser cannot reserve space, so the page jumps as images load.
checks.fix: Add width and height attributes that match the image's own size, and let CSS scale it.

findings.detail: 1 image lacks a width or height attribute.

checks.title: Images below the fold are not lazy loaded
checks.why: Images far down the page compete with the content visitors see first.
checks.fix: Add loading="lazy" to images that start below the first screen.

checks.title: Large JPEG or PNG
checks.why: Modern formats such as WebP and AVIF are often smaller at the same quality.
checks.fix: Convert the image to WebP or AVIF, and keep the old format as a fallback only if needed.

findings.detail: The image/png image is 600000 bytes.

checks.title: Render-blocking script in the head
checks.why: A script in the head without async or defer stops the browser from showing the page until it has loaded and run.
checks.fix: Add defer, or async for independent scripts, or move the script to the end of the body.

findings.detail: 1 script in the head blocks rendering.

checks.title: Many stylesheets in the head
checks.why: The browser waits for every stylesheet in the head before it draws the page.
checks.fix: Combine stylesheets, or inline the critical rules and load the rest later.

checks.title: Image without an alt attribute
checks.why: Screen readers have nothing to say about an image with no alt attribute, and may read out the file name instead.
checks.fix: Add an alt attribute that describes the image. Use alt="" for images that are only decoration.

findings.detail: 1 image has no alt attribute.

checks.title: Form control without a label
checks.why: People using screen readers cannot tell what a field is for, and a label also gives a larger target to click.
checks.fix: Add a label element that points at the field, or an aria-label or aria-labelledby attribute.

findings.detail: 1 form control has no label.

checks.title: Link without an accessible name
checks.why: A link with no text, label or image alt is announced as just link, so people using screen readers cannot tell where it goes.
checks.fix: Add link text, or an aria-label, or alt text on the image inside the link.

checks.title: Generic link text
checks.why: People who move through a page by its links hear them out of context, so click here and read more tell them nothing.
checks.fix: Write link text that says where the link goes or what it does.

findings.detail: 1 link uses generic text such as click here.

checks.title: Button without an accessible name
checks.why: A button with no text or label is announced as just button, so people using screen readers cannot tell what it does.
checks.fix: Add text inside the button, or an aria-label.

checks.title: Heading levels are skipped
checks.why: People who move through a page by its headings expect the levels to nest, and a gap suggests missing content.
checks.fix: Use the next heading level down, and pick levels for structure and not for size.

findings.detail: 1 heading level is skipped.

checks.title: Iframe without a title
checks.why: Screen readers announce an iframe by its title, so without one people cannot tell what the embedded content is.
checks.fix: Add a short title attribute that says what the frame contains.
